headline: Hardened it — tried hard to break it, then fixed what broke
note: Spent this session trying to make it fail the way it would in the wild: corrupted settings, glitchy input samples, garbage in every knob, odd channel counts, in-place buffers, weird sample rates. Found five ways to make the audio engine spit out NaN — which inside Windows' audio service is a loud click at best. All fixed with layered scrubbing: nothing non-finite can now reach your speakers. A corrupted settings file no longer crashes system audio, no longer mutes, and recovers the instant good settings return. The app also survives a totally garbled settings file on launch. Normal sound is untouched — bypass measures exactly 0.00 dB.
updated: hardening pass - 20 adversarial tests, all pass

items.text: Fuzzed the DSP: 13 categories, found 5 NaN paths
Output scrub - no NaN/Inf ever reaches audiodg
Input scrub - a bad sample can't poison a filter forever
Every setting clamped finite + in-range before it hits a filter
Corrupt settings file: no crash, no mute, full recovery
App survives empty/garbage/truncated state.json on launch
Odd channels, in-place, 44/96/192kHz, rapid toggling all clean
Surround/stereo decision now sticky - no popping on quiet film scenes
Regression: normal audio + effects still exact (bypass 0.00, gain -6.00)
Hardened DLL shipped in app + installer, running now
For you: the 30-ideas list - we'll pick from it once base is proven by ear
